patternAnalysis.whatIsThisPattern: Arrays store data in a straight line where every element has an index. Most array problems are about moving through the array smartly and using indexes correctly.
patternAnalysis.whenToUseThisPattern: Use arrays when you need fast access to elements and when order of data matters.
patternAnalysis.whenNotToUseThisPattern: Avoid arrays when you need to insert or delete elements frequently in the middle.
mentalChecklist: Can I solve this by scanning the array once?
Can I avoid using extra space?
Am I handling edge cases like empty array?
commonMistakes: Using extra space when not needed
patternAnalysis.timeComplexity: Most array problems run in O(n) time
patternAnalysis.spaceComplexity: O(1) if solved in-place, otherwise O(n)

patternAnalysis.whatIsThisPattern: Strings are sequences of characters. Most string problems are about comparing characters, moving pointers, or building a new string carefully.
patternAnalysis.whenToUseThisPattern: Use string techniques when the problem talks about characters, words, matching, or formatting text.
patternAnalysis.whenNotToUseThisPattern: Avoid complex string operations when a simpler numeric or array-based approach is enough.
mentalChecklist: Do I need to ignore spaces or cases?
Can I solve this in one pass?
Should I build a new string or modify logic?
commonMistakes: Forgetting to handle spaces or special characters
Missing edge cases like empty strings
patternAnalysis.timeComplexity: Most string problems run in O(n) time
patternAnalysis.spaceComplexity: O(1) for pointer-based solutions, O(n) if creating new strings

patternAnalysis.whatIsThisPattern: Bit manipulation means solving problems by working directly with binary bits instead of normal numbers.
patternAnalysis.whenToUseThisPattern: Use bit manipulation when the problem talks about bits, binary numbers, or when you want very fast and memory-efficient solutions.
patternAnalysis.whenNotToUseThisPattern: Avoid bit tricks if a simple math or array solution is easier to understand and works well.
mentalChecklist: Can I check or flip a bit?
Is there a repeating pattern in bits?
Can shifting bits simplify the problem?
Am I handling negative numbers correctly?
patternAnalysis.timeComplexity: Most bit manipulation solutions run in O(1) or O(n)
patternAnalysis.spaceComplexity: Usually O(1)

patternAnalysis.whatIsThisPattern: Hash tables store data as key-value pairs so we can find things very quickly.
patternAnalysis.whenToUseThisPattern: Use hash tables when you need fast lookup, counting, or checking if something already exists.
patternAnalysis.whenNotToUseThisPattern: Avoid hash tables when order matters or when a simple loop is enough.
mentalChecklist: Do I need to store counts?
Can a map simplify this logic?
Am I updating the map correctly?
commonMistakes: Assuming order in a hash map

patternAnalysis.whenToUseThisPattern: Use two pointers when the data is sorted or when you need to compare elements from both ends.

patternAnalysis.whatIsThisPattern: Prefix sum means storing running totals so you don’t have to recalculate sums again and again.
patternAnalysis.whenToUseThisPattern: Use prefix sums when the problem asks about subarray sums or range calculations.
patternAnalysis.whenNotToUseThisPattern: Avoid prefix sums if you only need a single calculation or simple traversal.
mentalChecklist: Do I need fast range queries?
Can a hash map help with prefix sums?
Am I handling negative numbers correctly?
Did I initialize prefix sum properly?

patternAnalysis.whatIsThisPattern: Kadane’s Algorithm finds the best subarray sum by deciding at every step whether to continue or start fresh.
patternAnalysis.whenToUseThisPattern: Use Kadane’s Algorithm when the problem asks for maximum sum, profit, or score in a continuous subarray.
patternAnalysis.whenNotToUseThisPattern: Avoid Kadane’s approach if the problem does not involve contiguous elements.
mentalChecklist: Should I continue the current subarray?
Should I start a new subarray here?
Am I tracking the global maximum?
Do negative values affect the result?
Do I need min value tracking as well?
commonMistakes: Resetting sum too late or too early
